rationale: Oversized diff limits full coverage; all four lenses ran cleanly. Nine blocking findings: download_file accumulates the entire response in heap with no size cap (CR-003), config_path resolves to a wrong path on Windows without HOME (CR-002), Windows executables bundled unconditionally into macOS DMG (CR-007), runProbe filters by deleted step IDs always returning empty (CR-008), self_update_direct awaits node.exe with no timeout (CR-006), codemie.cmd has no existence guard (CR-001), global_version detection deviates from spec with no injectable mock and no test assertion (CR-004), spawn_pty has no concurrent-occupancy guard (CR-005), and five commits violate git-workflow.md format (CR-009). Seven candidates dismissed after source verification confirmed guards present in current HEAD; two spec items partial on global_version detection method and handshake test coverage.

findings.title: Shim invokes bundled paths without existence check
findings.problem: codemie.cmd calls node.exe and the CLI JS unconditionally with no prior check that either file exists; if either bundled file is absent Windows emits a cryptic 'system cannot find the path' error with no installer-level context.
findings.impact: A corrupted or partial installation fails with an opaque OS error, giving users no indication of which component is missing or how to recover.
findings.recommendation: Add `if not exist "%BUNDLE_DIR%\node\node.exe" (echo INSTALLER ERROR: bundled node.exe not found & exit /b 1)` before the invocation line, and a matching check for the CLI JS entry-point.

findings.title: config_path ignores USERPROFILE on Windows
findings.problem: config_path() uses std::env::var("HOME").unwrap_or_default() only; Windows does not guarantee HOME (USERPROFILE is the standard), so on stock Windows the path resolves to '/.codemie/codemie-cli.config.json' and the file is never found.
findings.impact: read_codemie_config always returns CodemieConfig::default() (state=no-configuration) on Windows without HOME set (e.g. Windows Sandbox, stock Windows without Git for Windows), showing 'CodeMie Desktop' even when a valid config exists.
findings.recommendation: Use std::env::var("HOME").or_else(|_| std::env::var("USERPROFILE")).unwrap_or_default(), or a #[cfg(windows)] branch; add a test that exercises config_path() with USERPROFILE set.

findings.title: Download buffers full response in heap before write
findings.problem: download_file pre-allocates Vec::with_capacity from the untrusted Content-Length (u64 cast to usize) with no cap, then accumulates all chunks before calling tokio::fs::write; documented binaries are 165-170 MB. An adversarially large Content-Length can exhaust address space before any data reaches disk.
findings.impact: OOM or process panic on memory-constrained devices for legitimate large downloads; a server sending a maliciously inflated Content-Length can crash the installer before the download completes.
findings.recommendation: Cap the pre-allocation (e.g. .min(512 * 1024 * 1024)); restore chunk-by-chunk streaming write (AsyncWriteExt::write_all per chunk) or hash incrementally so peak heap usage is bounded regardless of payload size.

findings.title: Version subprocess not injectable; global_version untested
findings.problem: detect_handshake_state calls std::process::Command::new("codemie") directly at line 60 (not via an injectable abstraction); the spec required populating global_version via check_codemie_version logic (inspector.rs:93-96). No test asserts global_version on the found path; the subprocess cannot be mocked.
findings.impact: The version detection branch is never exercised by the test suite; a CI run without codemie on PATH silently skips version-detection coverage; divergence from the specified method may produce different semantics for edge-case version strings.
findings.recommendation: Extract the subprocess call behind an injectable closure (matching the probe parameter pattern); add a test asserting global_version = Some("2.0.1") when the mock subprocess returns "codemie v2.0.1".

findings.title: spawn_pty overwrites active PTY slot without killing prior child
findings.problem: spawn_pty writes to state.pty unconditionally at lines 109-120; a second call while a child is running overwrites the slot without killing the prior child. The prior child's wait-thread continues emitting engine:pty-exit events with the old run_id; pty_kill then operates on the new slot's killer instead.
findings.impact: Concurrent or retried PTY calls leak a process, emit stale exit events, and misdirect kills; reachability is uncertain under normal single-engine flow but no guard prevents it at the API level.
findings.recommendation: At the top of spawn_pty check if state.pty.lock().unwrap().is_some() and return Err(InstallerError::Pty("PTY already active".into())) to enforce the single-occupancy invariant explicitly.

findings.title: self_update_direct awaits node.exe with no timeout
findings.problem: tokio::process::Command::output().await in self_update_direct has no timeout wrapper; if the bundled node.exe stalls on startup the future never resolves.
findings.impact: The run_self_update IPC call blocks indefinitely; the UI spinner hangs with no recovery path, requiring a force-quit.
findings.recommendation: Wrap with tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(120), Command::new(node_exe).args([...]).output()).await and map a timeout into InstallerError::Other("self-update timed out".into()).

findings.title: Windows-only executables bundled into macOS DMG unconditionally
findings.problem: bundle.resources maps codemie.cmd and node.exe unconditionally; tauri.conf.json is platform-agnostic so both Windows-only artifacts are included in the macOS DMG as well as the NSIS installer.
findings.impact: macOS DMG carries unnecessary Windows executables (~70 MB node.exe + batch shim), increasing bundle size and potentially triggering macOS security scanning against a foreign PE binary embedded in the app bundle.
findings.recommendation: Use Tauri 2.x platform-conditional resource configuration to restrict codemie.cmd and node.exe to the nsis target only; leave only cli/node_modules in the macOS bundle.

findings.title: runProbe filters engine steps by deleted step IDs — always empty
findings.problem: runProbe sets safe = new Set(['1.1','1.1.1','1.2','1.2.1','1.3']) and filters engine.steps against it; after the YAML change engine.steps only contains 2.x IDs, so the filter returns [] and engine.run() completes with zero steps.
findings.impact: CODEMIE_PROBE_SMOKE=1 emits PROBE_RESULT with an empty string and exits; the probe always passes without exercising any step, giving testers a false green on runtime detection.
findings.recommendation: Update safe to new Set(['2.3.3','2.3.5','2.4']) to match the current step YAML; add a guard asserting steps.length > 0 before calling engine.run().

findings.title: Five commits violate git-workflow.md commit-format standard
findings.problem: git-workflow.md anti-patterns section explicitly forbids scope notation and requires plain '<type>: <description>'. Four commits use '(EPMCDME-14505)' as a parenthesised scope suffix. One commit uses a branch slug as the type token with no recognised conventional type.
findings.impact: Non-conforming commit history violates the documented project standard; automated changelog or release tools relying on conventional-commit parsing will fail or misclassify these entries.
findings.recommendation: Reword via interactive rebase: drop the parenthesised scope from the four scoped commits (e.g. 'feat: add check_handshake_state IPC command'); reword the branch-slug commit to 'chore: EPMCDME-14573 planning artifacts'.
